root_cause.text: The bounds check on DEFAULT_TABLE entries in verify_dfa() was incorrectly conditioned on the MATCH_FLAG_DIFF_ENCODE flag, so when a state uses differential encoding, the DEFAULT_TABLE entry is used as an array index without validation, enabling out-of-bounds reads/writes from a malformed DFA.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states "The verify_dfa() function only checks DEFAULT_TABLE bounds when the state is not differentially encoded. When the verification loop traverses the differential encoding chain, it reads k = DEFAULT_TABLE[j] and uses k as an array index without validation." The patch removes the `if (!(BASE_TABLE(dfa)[i] & MATCH_FLAG_DIFF_ENCODE) &&` condition to make the bounds check unconditional.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix DFA verification to check default state bounds for all states and log an error when out of bounds.
intent_record.what: Removed the condition `! (BASE_TABLE(dfa)[i] & MATCH_FLAG_DIFF_ENCODE)` from the if statement that checks if DEFAULT_TABLE(dfa)[i] >= state_count, and added a pr_err message before the goto out.
intent_record.how: The change makes the bounds check for the default state index unconditional (previously it was only checked when the MATCH_FLAG_DIFF_ENCODE flag was not set) and logs an error message when an out-of-bounds default state is encountered, which aids debugging.
